_readme: Calibration sets (COLLECTION.md §4) for Spark Capital, pre-registered 2026-09-05 BEFORE the base build (PRO-85 Phase 1). Two sets: `membership` (trap and known-true rows: slug -> [verdict, basis, evidence class]) and `stage` (entry-round golden key: slug -> {stage, entry_year, basis, citation}). Every stage answer rests on a document that names the round and Spark Capital's participation; web-verified 2026-09-05. Keys are the slugs the base is expected to carry (site rendering / slug_of(name)); a key that lands under another slug is re-pointed, never re-judged.
_stage_readme: stage: Pre-Seed | Seed | Series A | Growth (Series B and later, secondaries, tenders, at-scale entries). entry_year: the year Spark first put fund money in. basis: the document(s) the label rests on. citation: the document.

twitter: site-listed every era 2008-2026; Series B 2008 (Bijan Sabet board seat, Form D director 2009-2010); Spark Capital II 13G/13D on TWITTER, INC. 2014-2015
tumblr: site-listed 2007-2026; seed 2007 with USV; Form D director (Sabet) 2010-2011
boxee: site-listed 2008-2015; $4M Series A 2008 (Spark + USV); Form D director (Sabet) 2009-2011
cruise: site-listed 2015-2026; Series A 2015 co-led by Spark (Nabeel Hyatt director 2015)
anthropic: site-listed 2023-2026; Series C 2023 led by Spark (Razavi board seat)
deel: site-listed 2021-2026; Series B 2020 led by Spark; Form D director (Razavi) 2020-2023
talkspace: legal-name trap: the Form D issuer 'Groop Internet Platform Inc.' (Finkelstein director 2016-2019) is Talkspace, site-listed 2014-2026 and a fund 13G filer subject (Talkspace, Inc. 2021-2023)
wayfair: site-listed 2011-2026 (csn_stores 2011); $165M 2011 round; Finkelstein Form D director on WAYFAIR LLC 2012; fund Forms 3/4 and 13G 2014-2016
conduit-labs-inc: Nabeel Hyatt's own company (Executive Officer, 2009 Form D) before he joined Spark in 2012: founder-era paper, no Spark vehicle (D8 seat dating); acquired by Zynga 2010
skky-inc: 'Andrew Parker' Executive Officer 2013-2015 at SKKY Inc / SKKY, LLC: a homonym founder, no Spark listing
imperfect-foods-inc: Benjamin Simon (Executive Officer 2015-2017) is Imperfect Foods' co-founder, not the Spark 2022 team member of the same name; never Spark-listed
williamson-surgery-center-llc: 'Dennis Miller' director 2009: homonym of Spark's 2005-2011 general partner on a surgery-center LLC
blaze-bioscience-inc: 'Dennis Miller' Executive Officer 2014-2020 (a biotech CFO) — Spark's Dennis Miller left in 2011 and the firm never listed Blaze
medallion-resources-ltd: 'David Haber' director 2010-2020 on a Canadian mining issuer: homonym
shareaholic-inc: Rob Go's 2012-2014 seat is a NextView Ventures seat (he co-founded NextView after leaving Spark in 2010); never Spark-listed
printeco-inc: Arpan Shah as Executive Officer 2010-2011, a decade before he joined Spark (2025): his own company
searchmedia-holdings-ltd: 'Paul Conway' director 2012 on a Chinese advertising issuer: homonym
meadow-bay-capital-corp: 'Bill Reed' director 2011 on a Canadian shell: homonym; Spark's Will Reed joined in 2015
tradiv-inc: 'Geoff Doran' 2015-2016: homonym of Spark CFO Jeff Doran; an operations officer never sits issuer boards for the firm
mandalay-digital-group-inc: Spark's 13D on Mandalay Media (2008) is sale consideration from Mandalay's acquisition of Spark-backed Twistbox; the investment row is Twistbox (§1 consideration rule)
bond-street: founder-seat trap that IS a member: David Haber left Spark (2013) to found Bond Street, but the firm listed Bond Street on its 2015 site (/portfolio/bond-street/, /companies/bond-street/) as a portfolio company — the site listing suffices; Haber's Executive Officer seat is the founder's, not the firm's
papa-technologies-llc: 'Andrew Parker' as Executive Officer 2017-2021 is Papa's founder Andrew Parker, a homonym of Spark's partner (who left in 2019/2020); Papa was never Spark-listed
wei-chuan-u-s-a-inc: 'Charles Huang' director 2011 on a Taiwanese food importer: homonym of Spark's 2010-2011 associate
cnet: CNET (founded 1992, public 1996, acquired by CBS 2008) predates the 2005 firm; the 2008 Forms 3/4 and the 2021-2025 Webflow card are a partner's prior-firm track record shown on the site, not a Spark fund position (T2, D6)

tumblr.basis: Wikipedia (Tumblr): first round October 2007, $750,000 from Spark Capital and Union Square Ventures; the firm's own 2009 news page repeats 'some of their own seed funding like $300,000 in Tumblr'

twitter.basis: Twitter blog 2008-06-24 'Welcoming Bijan and Jeff': the Series B ($15M, May/June 2008) brought in Spark Capital (Bijan Sabet, board seat) and Bezos Expeditions; USV led the 2007 Series A. Series B = Growth by taxonomy

plaid.basis: Wikipedia (Plaid Inc.): September 2013 $2.8M seed round led by Spark Capital with Google Ventures and NEA; the Series A (Nov 2014, $12.5M) was led by NEA. The issue's 'Series A 2013 (Spark led)' was wrong: Spark's entry is the seed

oculus.basis: June 2013 $16M Series A co-led by Spark Capital (Santo Politi to the board) and Matrix Partners; the $75M Series B (Dec 2013) was a16z's; acquired by Facebook March 2014 ($2B)

cruise.basis: TechCrunch 2015-09-18: $12.5M Series A co-led by Spark Capital and Sam Altman; the issue's '2014' was wrong (the round closed September 2015); acquired by GM March 2016

postmates.basis: TechCrunch / PRWeb 2014-02-18: $16M Series B led by Spark Capital (Nabeel Hyatt to the board); Series B = Growth by taxonomy

anthropic.basis: Anthropic 2023-05-23: $450M Series C led by Spark Capital (Yasmin Razavi to the board), ~$4.5B post-money

trello.basis: TechCrunch 2014-07-24: $10.3M Series A led by Spark Capital and Index Ventures at the spin-out from Fog Creek (Bijan Sabet to the board)

kik.basis: TechCrunch 2011-03-07: $8M Series A from RRE Ventures, Spark Capital and Union Square Ventures (the firm's own news archive carries the VentureBeat repost)

slack.basis: TechCrunch 2015-04-16: $160M Series E at $2.8B with Spark Capital Growth among the new investors; the firm's 2018 site: 'partner with Slack through Spark Growth in 2015'

wayfair.basis: Wikipedia (Wayfair): June 2011 $165M round from Battery Ventures, Great Hill Partners, HarbourVest Partners and Spark Capital — the first outside capital into a nine-year-old, ~$500M-revenue business (the firm's own news archive: 'online home furnishings retailer csn stores raises 165 million'); an at-scale entry, keyed Growth although the press labelled it Series A (raised for Erik in the report as a label-vs-scale question)

affirm.basis: TechCrunch 2015-05-06: $275M equity and debt led by Spark Capital Growth (new investors Jefferies, a16z; existing Khosla, Lightspeed) at a $576M valuation — the company's Series B; Growth by taxonomy

carta.basis: FinSMEs 2015-01: eShares (renamed Carta 2017) $7M Series A led by Union Square Ventures with Spark Capital participating — Spark's first position; the Series B ($17M, Aug 2015) followed

flywire.basis: TechCrunch 2011-08-15: peerTransfer (renamed Flywire) $7.5M Series A led by Spark Capital with Accel, Maveron and Boston Seed; the $1.1M seed of Oct 2010 predates Spark

cybereason.basis: TechCrunch 2015-05-06 / company press release: $25M Series B led by Spark Capital (Santo Politi to the board) with CRV and Lockheed Martin; Series B = Growth

andela.basis: TechCabal / PE Hub 2015-06-25: $10M Series A led by Spark Capital (Spark's first Africa investment), SEC filing shows $14.6M

niantic.basis: TechCrunch 2017-11-24: $200M Series B led by Spark Capital (Megan Quinn to the board) with Founders Fund, Meritech, Javelin, You & Mr Jones, NetEase; Series B = Growth

deel.basis: TechCrunch / Business Wire 2020-09-09: $30M Series B led by Spark Capital (Yasmin Razavi) four months after the a16z-led $14M Series A; Series B = Growth

coinbase.basis: TechCrunch 2017-08-10: $100M Series D led by IVP with Spark Capital, Greylock, Battery, Section 32 and Draper participating — Spark's first Coinbase position (no earlier round names the firm); Series D = Growth

boxee.basis: TechCrunch 2008-11-18: $4M first institutional round split 50/50 between Spark Capital (Bijan Sabet to the board) and Union Square Ventures; the firm's own 2008 news page carries the story

5min-media.basis: TechCrunch 2007-11-01: $5M Series A from Spark Capital after a painful angel round (announced Jan 2008); the $7.5M second round (Jul 2009) followed; acquired by AOL 2010

aviary.basis: FinSMEs / AllThingsD 2009-10-26: $7M Series B led by Spark Capital (Mo Koyfman to the board) with existing investor Bezos Expeditions — Spark's entry at the B; Growth by taxonomy

wealthfront.basis: Business Wire 2014-10-28: $64M round led by Spark Capital Growth (Jeremy Philips) at a $700M valuation with Dragoneer and the existing investors; the company's Series D

handshake.basis: TechCrunch / EdSurge 2016-11-17: $20M Series B led by Spark Capital (Megan Quinn to the board) with KPCB, True and Annox; Series B = Growth

foursquare.basis: TechCrunch 2011-06-24: $50M Series C at $600M led by a16z with Spark Capital as a new investor (USV, O'Reilly existing); Spark later bought ~$50M of employee stock (2013 secondary). Series C = Growth

pendo.basis: Pendo press release 2016: $20M Series B led by Spark Capital; Series B = Growth

quantopian.basis: Crunchbase seed round profile / Tracxn: $2.1M seed, January 2012, led by Spark Capital (Andrew Parker); the Oct 2013 $6.7M Series A (GlobeNewswire) names Spark as the existing investor beside Khosla — the key follows the first check

academia-edu.basis: TechCrunch 2011-11-30: $4.5M Series A led by Spark Capital with True Ventures — the company's second round after a $2.2M 2009 round whose named investors are angels (Shuttleworth, Lehrman, Pennant-Rea); Spark's first listing of the company is the 2011 site

ramp.basis: Ramp blog 2021-08 (Series C, $300M at $3.9B) with Spark Capital among the investors; Tracxn dates Spark's first Ramp position to the Series C (2021-08-06). Growth by taxonomy

chainguard.basis: PR Newswire / company post 2023-11-01: $61M Series B led by Spark Capital with Sequoia, Amplify, Mantis and Banana Capital; Series B = Growth

lightmatter.basis: FinSMEs 2019-02: the $22M Series A-1 led by GV with Spark Capital and Matrix followed the $11M first Series A tranche of December 2017 from Matrix Partners and Spark Capital — Spark's entry is the 2017 Series A

abridge.basis: Business Wire 2023-10-26: $30M Series B led by Spark Capital at a $200M valuation with Bessemer and the health-system investors; Series B = Growth

etoro.basis: TechCrunch / PR Newswire 2011-01-26: $8.3M round led by Spark Capital with Social Leverage and existing investors — eToro's Series C (Spark's first position); the $15M 2012 round was Spark-led too. Growth by taxonomy

matx.basis: TechCrunch 2024-11-22: ~$80M Series A led by Spark Capital (Yasmin Razavi to the board; Form D director 2024-2026) at a low-$300M post-money; the $25M seed (2023) was led by Nat Friedman and Daniel Gross without Spark

warby-parker.basis: Crunchbase / news.crunchbase funding history: Spark's first Warby Parker position is the January 2013 Series B (the Sept 2012 $41.5M Series B was led by General Catalyst; Tiger led the 2011 Series A) — Growth by taxonomy; the 2013 site lists warby-parker

marqeta.basis: TechCrunch 2019-05-21: $260M Series E led by Coatue with Spark Capital among the new investors — Spark's first Marqeta position; Growth

kalshi.basis: Kalshi news 2025-10: $300M Series D at $5B co-led by a16z and Sequoia with Spark Capital among the participants — Spark's first Kalshi position (no earlier round names the firm); Growth

glossier.basis: PR Newswire 2019-03-19: $100M Series D led by Sequoia with Tiger Global, Spark Capital, Forerunner, Thrive, IVP and Index — Spark's first Glossier position; Growth

skillshare.basis: Gigaom 2011-08-16: $3.1M Series A from Union Square Ventures and Spark Capital four months after launch; the 2014 $6M (USV, Spark) and 2016 $12M rounds followed

mark43.basis: PR Newswire 2013-07-15: $1.95M seed from lead investors Spark Capital and General Catalyst (Alex Finkelstein a Form D director from 2013); the $10.8M Series A followed in Aug 2015

admeld.basis: PitchBook / company history: $7M Series A (June 2008) from Spark Capital and Foundry Group — AdMeld's first round; the firm's own news page carries the Norwest-led $15M Series C (2010); acquired by Google 2011 (~$400M)

next-new-networks.basis: TechCrunch 2007: launched March 2007 with $8M from Spark Capital, Saban Media, Pilot Group and Bob Pittman — the first institutional round (Series A by convention); the 2008 $15M round was Velocity/Goldman; acquired by YouTube 2011

stack-overflow.basis: TechCrunch 2011-03-08: $12M Series B led by Index Ventures with Spark Capital (Bijan Sabet to the board) and Union Square Ventures; USV had led the 2010 Series A. Series B = Growth

veoh-networks.basis: Hollywood Reporter / Adweek April 2006: $12.5M Series B from Michael Eisner, Spark Capital, Time Warner and existing investor Shelter Capital — Spark's entry at the B (Growth); one of the firm's first deals, on the 2006 site

_build_filtered_traps._note: trap keys the build removed before any verdict could be written (the correct outcome for each): 68-southbridge-llc = non-portfolio industry (Residential) with Form D as the only evidence; setpoint-technologies-inc, paintzen-inc, framer-inc = an ex-partner's seat 4+ years after the last site capture is the only evidence (tenure filter); spark-capital-iii-lp = pooled investment fund (own vehicle). Scored as not_member-equivalent on the gate.

paintzen-inc: Rob Go NextView-era seat 2014-2016; not Spark-listed

_layer_scores.scored: 2026-09-05, before the grind (COLLECTION.md §4: the gate calibrates layers, not only the judge)
_layer_scores.judge_blind_pass: 44/44 stage, 44/44 entry_year from the evidence pack plus parametric memory (scratch/gate-blind-pass.json); the pack alone would have diverged on 6 rows (Carta, Flywire, Lightmatter, Abridge, eToro, AdMeld) where the first partner-anchored Form D is a LATER round than the documented entry — the first filed round is a ceiling on entry recency, not the entry (§6)
_layer_scores.site_stage_label_2015_2020: 24/33 against the key (scratch: 'venture' fails one-directionally on Growth entries: Twitter, Postmates, Wayfair, Cybereason, Aviary, Foursquare, eToro, Warby Parker read 'venture'; AdMeld reads 'seed' for a Series A). Promoted to CORROBORATION for 'seed' (5/5) and 'growth' (8/8) values only; 'venture' is not a stage claim (18/20 as Series A, but the two misses are Growth entries labelled venture, so it never publishes)
_layer_scores.formd_band: 15/24 against the key: misses in both directions (Oculus, Carta, Andela, MatX read Growth for Series A entries because the first partner-anchored filing is a later round or an at-scale A; Flywire and Boxee read Seed for Series A rounds under $7M; Handshake, Pendo and eToro read Series A for Series B/C rounds of $8-22M). Kept as a ceiling on entry recency and as corroboration; never a label; every formd_band pre-fill is re-judged (§8 Black Forest Labs class)
_layer_scores.firm_news_archive_2006_2016: names the round on 11/44 golden rows (class 1 where it does: Boxee $4M, CSN Stores $165M, Cruise $12.5M, 5min $7.5M second round, Altius $8M A, Kik $8M, Admeld $15M C, ...); a recall and citation layer for the 2006-2016 book, not a coverage layer
_layer_scores.membership_traps: 26 keys in the base (11 known-true, 15 not_member) plus 5 build-filtered traps; the seed step marks site-listed rows member, so the two site-listed not_member traps (cnet: activist public stake shown as an alumni card; mandalay-media: the Twistbox acquirer listed as the successor) are seeded member and must be overridden by the judge in batch (recorded there as the gate's two seed-class exceptions)
